completion:
Inspect the bridge's external surfaces.
3. Pay attention to cracks and deformations.
4. Use appropriate measuring tools to quantify crack widths and lengths, as well as to measure deflections and vertical displacements.
5. Document rust, corrosion, and exposed reinforcing steel.
6. Look for spalling, delamination, and other damage to the concrete.
7. Assess the condition of the bearings and expansion joints.
8. Examine the bridge deck for potholes and general wear.
9. Check the drainage system for clogs and inefficiencies.
10. Note any damage to the railing, guardrail, and parapets.
11. Evaluate the substructure, including piers, abutments, and foundations, for erosion, scour, and signs of movement.
12. Utilize close-up photographs to document the defects. Ensure images are taken with good lighting, are in focus, and include scale references where necessary.
